name: Unreal past: as if, it's time, would rather
subtitle: Use a past tense for ideas that are not real now: He talks as if he owned the place. It's time we left. I'd rather you didn't smoke here.

flow.text: as if / it's time / would rather
past form, but the meaning is now

concept.exampleHtml: He talks as if he owned the place. — It's time we left. — I'd rather you didn't smoke here.

qa.html: as if / as though compares something with a situation that is not true. Use the past simple for the present: He talks as if he owned the place. (He doesn't own it.) Use the past perfect for the past: She looked as if she had seen a ghost. If the comparison is probably true, use the present: It looks as if it's going to rain. In speech, like is also common: It looks like it's going to rain.

It's time + subject + past simple means: we should do it now, and we have not done it yet. It's time we left. It's high time or about time is stronger and often shows impatience: It's high time you found a job. Without a new subject, use to + infinitive: It's time to leave.

would rather shows a preference. For your own action use the infinitive without to: I'd rather stay in tonight. I'd rather not go. For another person's action use the past simple: I'd rather you didn't smoke here. (now or later). For the past use the past perfect: I'd rather you had told me.

suppose / supposing / imagine start an unlikely situation. Use the past simple: Suppose you won a million pounds. What would you do? — Imagine you lived in Paris. Use the past perfect for the past: Suppose she had said no.
Typical mistakes: ✗ It's time we leave. → ✓ It's time we left. · ✗ I'd rather you don't smoke. → ✓ I'd rather you didn't smoke. · ✗ I'd rather to stay at home. → ✓ I'd rather stay at home. (no to)

concept.noteHtml: After as if the verb be is were in formal English (as if he were the boss). was is common in everyday speech. as though means the same as as if, but it sounds a little more formal. US: Americans often say like instead of as if: He acts like he owns the place. The same past-for-unreal idea appears with wish and if only: see Third and mixed conditionals; wish. For the basic conditionals, see Conditionals 0, 1, 2. For would as a modal, see Modal verbs.

tables.caption: The patterns
head: Pattern
Meaning
Example
rows: as if / as though + past simple
He acts {as if he owned} the place.
She looked {as if she had seen} a ghost.
It looks {as if it's going} to rain.
It's (high / about) time + subject + past simple
regret about someone else's past action

tables.caption: True or not true?
head: Sentence
What it tells you
rows: He talks as if he {were} a doctor.
Not true: he isn't a doctor.
She looked as if she {had seen} a ghost.
Not true: she hadn't seen a ghost.
He spends money as if it {grew} on trees.
Not true: money doesn't grow on trees.

items: I'd rather you left now. (now or later)
I'd rather you had left earlier. (past)
as if he knew (now) · as if he had known (before)
No to after would rather: I'd rather stay.
were is formal for all persons: as if I were…
Informal: like (It looks like it's going to rain.)

listen.text: He talks as if he owned the place.
listen.note: as if + past simple: it is not true. He doesn't own it.
It's high time + past simple: we should go now.

listen.text: I'd rather you didn't tell her.
listen.note: would rather + you + past simple: a preference about someone else.

hoeren.instruction: Listen and choose the words you hear. Listen for the verb form after as if, it's time and would rather.

items.text: She looks as if she had seen a ghost.

choices: It's time for we to leave

items.text: I'd rather stay at home tonight.
He acts as though he were the boss.
I'd rather you had told me earlier.

rounds.label: 1 · It's time we …
rounds.instruction: You hear a sentence with should. Say it again with It's time and the past simple.

items.answer: It's time you called your mother.
It's time they started the meeting.
It's time she made a decision.

items.prompt: I should buy a new phone.
items.answer: It's time I bought a new phone.
It's time he told the truth.

rounds.label: 2 · I'd rather you didn't …
rounds.instruction: You hear what someone might do. Say that you would prefer them not to.

example.answer: I'd rather you didn't smoke in the house.

items.prompt: You park in front of the house.
items.answer: I'd rather you didn't park in front of the house.
I'd rather you didn't phone me at work.
I'd rather you didn't tell Mum.
I'd rather you didn't use my laptop.
I'd rather you didn't bring the dog.
I'd rather you didn't open the window.

exercises.title: Probably true or not true?
exercises.hint: Past tense after as if = not true. Present tense = probably true.

exercises.title: Choose the right form.
exercises.hint: Unreal now: past simple. Unreal past: past perfect. After would rather (own action): infinitive without to.

exercises.title: Now or before?
exercises.hint: Now (unreal): past simple. Before (unreal): past perfect.

exercises.title: What goes together?
exercises.hint: Tap the situation, then the comparison that fits it.

exercises.title: Gap text: A message about the flat
exercises.hint: Which word or form fits each gap: time, rather, as if, a past form?
